idea.title: A staging Compose file is not a release procedure
idea.summary: A staging stack already had Compose services, backups, and monitoring, but still lacked a safe executable release path that tied an immutable image to backup, migration, readiness, smoke checks, and failure behavior.

context.goal: Create a small reusable staging deployment and rehearsal path without changing production behavior.
context.situation: The release candidate image had passed CI, security scanning, and runtime checks, while staging had no approved deployment command sequence.
context.problem: Existing Compose configuration alone did not establish image identity checks, migration ordering, failure handling, or an operator evidence trail.
context.investigation: Compared staging Compose, backup/restore operations, observability, and the production-only release script.
context.decision: Add a staging-only script and concise runbook that reuse existing services and block production identifiers.
context.implementation: The path verifies an immutable candidate image, takes a backup, stops the prior API before migrations, validates readiness, and does not automatically restore or restart an old API after migration begins.
context.result: A reviewable staging release path now exists without deploying staging or adding deployment infrastructure.

learning_points: Infrastructure configuration and an executable release procedure solve different problems.
Migration safety depends on making the old and new API ordering explicit.
A staging deployment tool can be small when it reuses existing backup, Compose, and health mechanisms.
story_points: The missing piece was not another platform, but a trustworthy sequence.
A pre-migration failure can safely restart the old API; a post-migration failure needs a different policy.
Immutable image identity belongs in operator tooling, not only in CI logs.
possible_angles: Why Docker Compose is not enough to make a release safe.
The release boundary that changes after a database migration starts.
How to turn a verified container image into a repeatable staging rehearsal.

notes: No secrets, infrastructure credentials, customer data, or private logs were captured.
